call.title: Cancellation call — Fieldnote Creative renewal increase

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Thank you for calling Open Gong, this is Elena. Before we get going — this call is recorded for quality purposes. What can I do for you today?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Hi Elena. This is Marcus Webb, I'm the founder of Fieldnote Creative. We're on your Growth plan. I'm calling to cancel our subscription.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Okay, I can help with that, Marcus. Can I verify the account email first?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: It's marcus@fieldnotecreative.com.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Got it, I have your account here. Before I process anything — would you mind telling me what's driving the decision?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Honestly? Price. Our renewal notice came through last week and the price has gone up thirty percent. That's a big jump for a fifteen-person agency.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: That's fair, and I appreciate you being direct about it. The thirty percent reflects the new Growth plan pricing, yes. Can I ask how your team actually uses Open Gong day to day?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: The account managers record their client calls and use the summaries. That part works well, no complaints. But we're also paying for a bunch of things we never touch.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Which parts feel like dead weight to you?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: The coaching scorecards, the deal pipeline view, the CRM sync — we don't use any of it. We're an agency, not a sales floor. I'd guess we use maybe half the product.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: So the real value for you is recording, transcripts, and the summaries — the core call documentation.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Exactly. And that's the other thing — a competitor called TalkTrace quoted us basically that feature set for about half of what your renewal comes to.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Do you mind sharing their number, so I'm comparing like with like?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: They quoted two hundred and ten a month for fifteen seats. Your renewal works out to four hundred and twenty.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Thank you, that's genuinely helpful. Can I ask a couple more questions before we talk about cancelling?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Of your fifteen seats, how many people actually record calls in a given month?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Probably eight or nine. The design side barely logs in.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Okay. And the summaries your account managers rely on — are those internal, or do they go to clients?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Both. The client-facing recaps are honestly the main reason we've kept it this long. Clients love them.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: That's useful to know. Here's why I'm asking — it sounds to me like you're on the wrong plan more than the wrong product. Growth bundles all the sales features you just listed as dead weight.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Well, it was the plan we were put on two years ago. Nobody's reviewed it since.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Right, and that's on us as much as anyone. There's a Core plan now — just recording, transcription, and summaries. It launched in the spring, so it didn't exist when you signed up.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Nobody has ever mentioned a Core plan to me.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: You're not the first person to say that this month. On Core, fifteen seats would come to two hundred and fifty-five a month. If we trimmed you to ten seats — covering the people who actually record — it's one hundred and seventy a month.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: One seventy. That's less than the TalkTrace quote.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: It is. And you'd keep everything the team already has — your call history, your client recap templates, your integration settings. Moving tools means re-training your account managers and starting the archive from zero.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Losing the history would sting, I'll give you that. We have about two years of client calls in there.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Two years of searchable client conversations is not a small thing to walk away from. Can I ask — is the decision final on your side, or is there a version of this where you stay?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: I'll be straight with you: I came into this call planning to cancel today. The thirty percent increase with no warning really annoyed me. It felt like being taken for granted.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: I hear you, and I'm sorry it landed that way. For what it's worth, that feedback goes to our pricing team — the renewal comms this cycle were not our best work.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Appreciated. Look, it's not personal, it's budget. We're fifteen people and every line item is under review this quarter.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Understood. So let me put two concrete options on the table. Option one: downgrade to Core at ten seats for one hundred and seventy a month, and you keep your whole archive. Option two: if you'd rather keep the full Growth feature set, I can apply a twenty percent renewal discount for the year, which brings it to three hundred and thirty-six a month.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: The Core option sounds a lot closer to what we actually need.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: That was my read too.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: But I'm not deciding on this call. I want to see the comparison in writing, and I need to run it past my ops lead — she manages the account managers day to day.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Completely reasonable. What would the comparison need to cover for it to be useful to her?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Exactly what we lose going from Growth to Core, feature by feature. And specifically — if the client recap templates don't survive the downgrade, this whole conversation is moot.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: The recap templates do carry over — they're part of Core, not a Growth add-on. But I'll put that in writing in the comparison so you're not just taking my word for it.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Good. Now, what about the renewal date? We renew on the twenty-eighth, and I don't want to get auto-billed at the new rate while I'm still thinking.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Fair. I'm placing a hold on your auto-renewal right now, so nothing bills on the twenty-eighth while you decide.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Okay. That helps.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: And I'll hold both offers — the Core pricing at one seventy and the twenty percent Growth discount — until the twenty-seventh. That gives you a full week to decide with the real numbers in front of you.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: A week is enough. What are you thinking, a call same time next week?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Next Thursday at this time works on my end. I'll send the comparison document tomorrow morning so you and your ops lead have it well before we talk.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Alright, book it. But Elena, I want to be clear — if the numbers don't work or the downgrade drops something we need, we're going with TalkTrace. This isn't a soft maybe.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Understood, and I'd rather you make that call with the real numbers in front of you than cancel today off a renewal letter. If Core doesn't fit, I'll process the cancellation myself on Thursday, no run-around.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: That's fair. I can work with that.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: While I have you — is there anything else that's been bugging the team about the product? If I'm sending feedback up, I'd rather send the full picture.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Honestly, the product itself has been fine. The mobile app is clunky, but that's a nitpick. This is a pricing conversation, not a product one.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Noted on the mobile app — that one does come up, and there's a rebuild in progress. Anything else on the billing or account side?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: No, the rest is fine. It really is just the money.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Okay. Let me recap so we're aligned. Your auto-renewal is on hold, so there's no charge on the twenty-eighth. I send you the Growth-to-Core comparison tomorrow morning, including written confirmation that the recap templates carry over. Both offers stand until the twenty-seventh. And we talk next Thursday at this same time.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: That matches what I've got written down.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Perfect. And Marcus — thank you for giving this a week instead of walking today. Genuinely.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Well, you earned the week. Most cancellation calls are twenty minutes of hold music and a survey at the end.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: We try to do a bit better than that. You'll have the document in your inbox tomorrow morning. Anything else I can do for you today?

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: No, that covers it.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Great. Talk next Thursday, Marcus.

lines.speaker: Marcus
lines.text: Talk then. Thanks, Elena. Bye.

fields.name: empathy_and_tone
fields.justification: Elena acknowledged the frustration directly, apologized for the renewal communication, and respected the customer's need to decide with his ops lead rather than pressuring for a same-call save. Slightly slow to acknowledge the emotional side — the first several minutes were diagnostic before the apology landed.

evidence.quote: I hear you, and I'm sorry it landed that way. For what it's worth, that feedback goes to our pricing team — the renewal comms this cycle were not our best work.
Completely reasonable. What would the comparison need to cover for it to be useful to her?

fields.justification: Strong save attempt: usage-based diagnosis led to a downgrade that undercuts the competitor quote, backed by a renewal hold, held pricing with a deadline, and a booked decision call. Not a 5 because the churn risk is real and unresolved — the outcome hinges on the comparison document and the ops lead's review.
